EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Former Jeremy Clarkson-Owned Ferrari F355 GTS Sells for Double the Auction Estimate
11 photos
Photo: Iconic Auctioneers
If there was need for further proof that being a celebrity pays off, then what follows is exactly that: a Ferrari F355 GTS bought new by Jeremy Clarkson, one of the most iconic figures in television, just sold for more than twice the money the guy selling it was hoping for.
Truth be told, the huge amount of cash spent on it (more on that in a bit) didn't go to Clarkson himself, as the man has long parted ways with the car, giving it as a prize to a reader of his Sunday Times columns some 26 years ago.
Since that time, it probably exchanged hands several times, and the current owner listed it for sale during the Iconic Auctioneers’ NEC Classic Motor Show Sales event last week. Someone bought it and set a live auction world record in the process.
Back when it announced the sale of the Rosso Corsa Prancing Horse , Iconic Auctioneers estimated it would go for between £200,000 and £250,000 (that's $263,000 to $329,000). Because the right guy was in the house when the Italian beauty went under the hammer, it ended up selling for £405,000 ($533,000), which is more than double the lower estimate.
We don't know who the buyer of the Ferrari is, but we do know what they got themselves earlier this month: a car packing its original V8 engine and six-speed manual, the factory-installed carbon-backed sports seats in Crema leather, and even the original order correspondence and the Warranty Card that proves the TV star was the vehicle's first owner.
With 15,200 miles (24,462 km) on the odometer, chassis number ZFFXR42C000106175 also comes complete with the original tool kit, red carpets, and the removable targa roof that makes this thing a true GTS.
In the time that has passed since it was purchased by Clarkson, the Ferrari was subjected to some restoration and repair work by its subsequent owners. That includes cosmetic tweaks, both inside and outside, steering rack repairs, and a cambelt replacement.
Bought new by Clarkson but no longer in his possession, the 1996 Ferrari F355 GTS didn't make the star any actual money this time. But the man did have his own vehicles listed for sale during the Iconic Auctioneers event, and they all lived up to their hype.
No less than three Clarkson-owned cars went under the hammer, achieving a combined £160,312 (around $211,000). First up is the 1982 Lancia Montecarlo Spider, the last car the man drove in The Grand Tour, which snatched £69,187 ($91,000), a live auction record as well.
The rest of the money comes from Clarkson also selling his 1983 Alfa Romeo GTV6 from The Grand Tour adventure that became known as ‘Well Aged Scotch ', and the 1978 Lincoln Continental Mark V that made an appearance in The Grand Tour Presents: Lochdown, a COVID-era special filmed in Scotland.
